# Idea card: Preprints with shorter titles collect more citations at two years because search engines retrieve them more often.

## Framing
Framing: approved by the user | Objective: Measure the retrieval effect of shortening a preprint title | Success criterion: Use paired index queries to distinguish title matching from venue reputation with adequate power | Constraints: Use an offline index containing public citation metadata | Would be refuted by: Paired title variants return identical ranks on the frozen index | Project archives: not checked (no project_dirs given): nothing is penalised
## Idea
Preprints with shorter titles collect more citations at two years because search engines retrieve them more often. If so, shortening titles is a cheap lever for visibility. | Gain that would justify the effort: Knowing whether title length acts through retrieval (a causal lever authors control) or only marks journal prestige (no lever). | Project numbers and the power: no project numbers were given: every power input is an assumed range, not a measured value.
